title: Residue projection gives a direct-image Tor window under a supplied relative bound
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, $R=\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring, $t$ a uniformizer, $n\geq1$, $A=R/t^nR$ and $\kappa=A/(t)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Assume explicitly that $A$ is a finite Noetherian commutative ring, meaning every ideal is finitely generated. Let $f:X\to Y$ be any scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme]. Use ordinary derived categories of constant-ring module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with constant sheaves $\kappa_X,\kappa_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Let $c\geq0$ be an integer such that $R^qf_*M=0$ for every $A$-module sheaf $M$ and every $q>c$. Let $a\leq b$ be integers and $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ have Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Assume $F=Rf_*K$ has bounded constructible cohomology. Then $F$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b+c]$; equivalently, for every degree-zero $A_Y$-module sheaf $N$, $\mathcal H^i(F\otimes_A^L N)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b+c]$. No finite-type, separatedness or base-field hypothesis is imposed on $f$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.17, residue-tensor/projection argument; abstract relative-bound form with constructibility assumed, extracted from returned parent Steps 4–5

proof.text: Extract an upper cohomological bound on K from its assumed bounded constructibility. For M = kappa, the quotient A/(t) is a finite A-module, hence finitely presented since A is Noetherian (Module.finitePresentation_of_finite). Test the Tor hypothesis on the constant residue sheaf to obtain L = K tensor^L kappa_X supported in [a,b]. No tensor-unit test is necessary.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.17, residue specialization of the finite-constant coefficient argument; explicit unit and quotient tests

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant] to the same scheme morphism $f$, coefficient ring $A$, bounded-above object $K$, finitely presented module $M=\kappa$ and natural bound $N=c.toNat$ (using $c\geq0$). Its Noetherian and higher-image hypotheses are exactly assumptions of the item. It gives an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$, $$F\otimes_A^L\kappa_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*L.$$ This does not require $\kappa$ to be flat or perfect over $A$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.17; abstract supplied-bound projection input stated by the cited node

proof.text: Use the existing Grothendieck-abelian, enough-injective and K-injective instances for ordinary ModuleCat-valued sheaves supplied by the source derived-category framework. The existing lowerStar functor is additive. Its unbounded right derivation is triangulated and commutes with shifts. For i < 0 use Functor.isGE_rightDerivedFunctor_obj_singleFunctor. For i > c, nonnegativity of c allows i = q for q natural; the isomorphism Functor.homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso, obtained from the plus/total comparison and the classical heart identification, transports the supplied classical higher-image vanishing. This bounds every heart image in [0,c], and also supplies the natural-number bound c.toNat required by finite-constant projection.

source.place: Tags 015A (definition-higher-derived-functors), 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing), 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived); unbounded comparison and triangulatedness as in the cited source-library nodes

proof.text: Convert the explicit cohomology vanishing for L into L.IsGE a and L.IsLE b, hence boundedness. Apply the already proved source-library DerivedCategory.isGE_obj_of_isGE to Rf_* with heart lower bound zero, and DerivedCategory.isLE_obj_of_isLE with heart upper bound c. These two finite truncation inductions give Rf_*L in [a,b+c]. Convert back using DerivedCategory.isGE_iff and isLE_iff. This is exactly the finite cohomology-triangle argument of Stacks 08J5; the more general class-restricted bounded_heart_amplitude wrapper is unnecessary because the class here is all module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle; proved source-library WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.TStructure, isGE_obj_of_isGE and isLE_obj_of_isLE (finite bounded-input truncation induction)

proof.text: The isomorphism of Step 2 and the vanishing of Step 4 show $\mathcal H^i(F\otimes_A^L\kappa_Y)=0$ outside $[a,b+c]$. Apply [lem-exc-residue-tor-test] to $T=Y$, the specified coefficients $A=\mathcal O_E/t^n$ and the object $F$, which has bounded constructible cohomology by assumption. It gives Tor amplitude $[a,b+c]$ for $F$. By [def-kun-tor-amplitude] this means the asserted vanishing after tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf $N$, including nonconstant ones. All geometry-dependent information was supplied as the bound $c$ and constructibility assumption, so no additional hypothesis on $f$ was used.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.17 residue-tensor argument; ordinary etale residue Tor test as stated by the cited node

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.7.17 motivates residue projection. Its geometric hypotheses are replaced here by the explicitly supplied relative bound and bounded constructibility; the finite bounded-heart argument follows Stacks 08J5 and 05TC, not a use of that lemma outside its hypotheses. B5 formalization: use bounded constructibility for the upper bound of K, ordinary module-valued sheaf instances and the existing unbounded single-object cohomology comparison. The finite bounded-heart argument and residue projection are unchanged. K2 pruning: use the proved source-library isGE_obj_of_isGE and isLE_obj_of_isLE finite devissage lemmas directly in Step 4; the class-restricted bounded-heart wrapper is not used. No mathematical route or public statement changes.
